question.text: This British Major General surrendered following the Siege of Yorktown.
question.clue: This man's most famous act was actually performed by a proxy, General Charles O'Hara, who surrendered to Benjamin Lincoln, the subordinate of George Washington.

swap.leadin: This battle saw the death of Joseph Warren.
swap.text: Name this Revolutionary War battle fought near Boston, mostly on nearby Breed's Hill.
swap.answerHtml: Battle of Bunker Hill [accept Battle of Breed’s Hill before mentioned]
swap.clue: In the prelude to this battle, British forces advanced on the Dorchester Neck leading Israel Putnam to prepare nearby defenses.

question.leadin: It included skirmishes at Freeman's Farm and Bemis Heights, and is commonly considered the turning point in the war.
question.text: Name this campaign to take New York, with American Revolutionary forces led by Horatio Gates.
question.clue: John Burgoyne surrendered to Horatio Gates after this campaign.

swap.leadin: Give the following about America's most famous pamphleteer, Thomas Paine.
swap.text: This 1776 work by Paine argues that no mother should treat her children as horribly as Britain had treated the American colonies; therefore, the colonies should declare independence.
swap.clue: Another chapter of this work claims that a certain monarch did little but "make war and give away places".

question.leadin: Answer the following about women to whom Vice Presidents were married.
question.text: This wife of the first Vice President told her husband John to "remember the ladies" while he was at the Continental Congress. This woman was also an outspoken anti-slavery advocate.
question.clue: This figure once called Alexander Hamilton "a man as ambitious as Julius Caesar" and regularly corresponded with Mercy Otis Warren, who congratulated this person on moving to an "elevated position" after this person left Quincy for Philadelphia.

swap.leadin: Cannons taken from this location were transported by Henry Knox to help relieve a siege.
swap.text: Name this fort on Lake Champlain that was captured by Ethan Allen's Green Mountain Boys in 1775 to almost no resistance.
swap.clue: This fort's location near Lake Champlain made it useful in monitoring trade routes between New York and Canada.

question.leadin: Georgia did not initially send delegates to this conference, though Lyman Hall came as a delegate from the Parish of St. John's.
question.text: Name this convention that served as the first national government of the United States. This body sent the Olive Branch Petition to King George III.
question.clue: A letter sent to a member of this body notes that "all men would be tyrants if they could" and urged this body to "Remember the Ladies."

swap.text: Cornwallis's surrender to the Americans at Yorktown basically marked the end of this war, which started at the battles of Lexington and Concord.
swap.clue: The Intolerable Acts precipitated this war, which involved an early battle at Bunker Hill.

question.text: The site at which Molly Pitcher manned the cannons for her husband, this June 1778 battle saw American General Charles Lee order a sudden retreat, for which he was later court-martialed. Forces under Generals Washington and von Steuben arrived and prevented a disastrous defeat. For 15 points-name this New Jersey battle.
question.clue: This battle ended the Philadelphia campaign, as Henry Clinton was commanded to evacuate to New York.

swap.leadin: This man was the godson of Horace Walpole and would go on to replace Philip Schuyler as the general in charge of American troops in New York.
swap.text: Identify this general who suffered a severe defeat at the Battle of Camden. With Benedict Arnold, he had earlier defeated John Burgoyne at the Battle of Saratoga.
swap.clue: This man's aide John Armstrong authored a letter to Washington demanding unfunded pensions in the Newburgh Conspiracy.

question.leadin: Name some things about the Revolutionary War in New Jersey.
question.text: This American general commanded an outnumbered forward guard at Monmouth and later took Stony Point. After the Revolution, he defeated Little Turtle and Blue Jacket at the Battle of Fallen Timbers.
question.clue: Following that victory against Blue Jacket, this man negotiated the Treaty of Greenville.

swap.text: One member of this family served as royal governor of New Jersey and was a key Loyalist leader during the Revolution. His father served the patriot cause as a minister to France and earlier published Poor Richard's Almanack.
swap.clue: This family, another member of which wrote articles for the New-England Courant under the pseudonym "Silence Dogood" and would go on to begin publishing the The Pennsylvania Gazette in 1728.

question.text: This revolutionary petitioned to free the enslaved man James Armistead after he spied on Benedict Arnold as a double agent. This subject of Mike Duncan's Hero of Two Worlds took an 1824 "grand tour" of the U.S.
question.answerHtml: Marquis de Lafayette [or Gilbert du Motier, Marquis de Lafayette; or Marie-Joseph Paul Yves Roch Gilbert du Motier, Marquis de La Fayette; accept James Armistead Lafayette; accept Hero of Two Worlds: The Marquis de Lafayette in the Age of Revolution]
question.clue: With the Comte de Mirabeau, this man drafted the Declaration of the Rights of Man, which was modeled after the Declaration of Independence.

swap.leadin: John Cadwalader shot this group's namesake in the mouth during a duel, declaring "I've stopped the damned rascal's tongue"
swap.text: Name this group led by a namesake Revolutionary War officer who sought to replace George Washington with Horatio Gates.
swap.clue: Another member of this group defeated Arthur St. Clair in a Pennsylvania gubernatorial election and John Cadwalader shot this group's namesake in the mouth in a duel.

question.leadin: During this event, one party made a speech stating that no one should try to "open the floodgates of civil discord and deluge our rising empire in blood."
question.text: Identify this event in which the Continental Army threatened the newly formed United States government due to uncertainty over them receiving their pensions. George Washington managed to quell it with a good short speech.
question.clue: It followed the rejection of an impost amendment supported by its possible real organizers, Robert Morris and Alexander Hamilton.

swap.text: During the Time of Troubles, Michael Romanov's Saltykov mother was forced to become a nun and adopt this name. A 15th-century "mayoress" with this name resisted Ivan III's siege of Novgorod.
swap.clue: While living on Cherry Street, a woman with this first name corresponded with Lucy Flucker Knox and hosted the son of the Marquis de Lafayette.

question.leadin: As part of a series of boycotts on British goods, colonial women in Massachusetts were encouraged to perform this action, rather than shopping.
question.text: A 1760s movement involved what action meant to harm British business in response to the Townshend Acts?
question.answerHtml: make clothing at home [accept textiles or other synonyms in place of clothes; accept descriptive answers indicating clothes are being made rather than purchased; accept making yarn; accept Homespun movement; prompt on answers like making things at home with “what is being made?”]

swap.leadin: This admiral failed to invade Jamaica after he lost the Battle of the Saintes to the British, but that happened after we won the Revolutionary War so who cares.
swap.text: Name this French admiral who had earlier defeated the British at the Battle of the Chesapeake and blockaded Yorktown.
swap.answerHtml: Comte de Grasse [or François Joseph Paul, Comte de Grasse, Marquis of Grasse-Tilly]

question.leadin: A conspiracy theory suggests this man was poisoned by a British spy named Edward Bancroft.
question.text: Name this first U.S. envoy to France. This Connecticut politician was recalled to the U.S. amid questions about his finances and was further embarrassed when his private letters suggesting the American Revolution was hopeless were published.
question.clue: Together with Benjamin Franklin and Dr. Arthur Lee, this Connecticut-born man became the first U.S. diplomat sent abroad when he went to France as a secret agent. He had been sent by the so-called Secret Committee, and met with the Comte de Vergennes in 1776 to secure munitions.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about crossdressing shenanigans during the Revolutionary War, FTPE.
swap.text: At around the same time, British lieutenant colonel Alexander Stewart gained a reputation for crossdressing in the wake of this 1781 battle, in which Nathaniel Greene forced Stewart to flee to Charleston about a month before Yorktown.
swap.clue: Often called the bloodiest battle of the Revolution, this September 1781 assault on Alexander Stewart deteriorated into a raid on the British wine supplies, but nonetheless trapped Stewart's forces in Charlestown for the rest of the war.
